gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Anker's 6,000 W rating for the SOLIX F3800 Plus needs an expansion battery: Anker's own footnote says one unit alone gives 3,300 W, which is less than one EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3 (4,000 W) or one Jackery Explorer 5000 Plus (7,200 W at 240 V).
standout_why: I read StormWatts (cited), EnergySage (cited), TheSolarLab (cited), Offset Solar (cited) and OutageReadyHQ (result 10). All of them print 6,000 W for the F3800 Plus as the unit's own output. EnergySage calls it '6,000 W continuous', and TheSolarLab gives both 2,600 W and 6,000 W without explaining either. None of them gives the 3,300 W single-unit figure. For cycle life, only StormWatts says what capacity each rating ends at (DELTA Pro 3 '4,000 to 80%', HomePower 3600 Plus '6,000 to 70%'), and it leaves the F3800 Plus figure as '3,000+' with no percentage. No rival puts the products' cycle ratings on one end-of-life basis. I could not open TheOutagePlan (cited) or SolarGenReview (cited): one failed its certificate check and the other returned HTTP 429. Either could already have the footnote.
decides: ChatGPT's second answer sells the F3800 Plus as 'Best for higher-power appliances' because of the 6,000 W figure. A shopper buying one box gets 3,300 W, which is below the DELTA Pro 3's 4,000 W at a similar price. So the DELTA Pro 3 is the better high-output single unit, and the F3800 Plus only earns its power claim once you add a BP3800 at $1,999.99 (the price on our current page; I could not re-check it today). The cycle footnote points the same way. EcoFlow rates the DELTA Pro 3 at 4,000 cycles to 80% capacity. Jackery rates the 5000 Plus at 4,000 cycles to 70%, and Anker gives no end point at all. On the makers' own terms, the DELTA Pro 3 makes the strongest durability promise of the three. This confirms the DELTA Pro 3 as the pick for most homes.

findings.label: AC output, single unit vs with expansion battery
findings.value: 3,300 W alone; 6,000 W only with 1 or more expansion batteries
findings.note: Footnote 1 on the spec table, verbatim: '3,300W for single unit, 6,000W when working with 1 or more expansion batteries'. The L14-30R line reads '120V/240V~ 25A Max, 60Hz, 6000W Max', and the standard 120 V outlets total 2,400 W max.

findings.label: 240 V output limit
findings.value: No 240 V output while the unit is charging from 120 V AC
findings.note: Verbatim: 'The 240V output cannot be used while the device is charging via 120V AC.'

findings.label: Cycle life
findings.note: The page says 'LFP, 3,000+ cycles' and '10+ years of lifespan and 5-year warranty'. It does not say what capacity remains at the end of those cycles, so this figure can't be compared directly with the 80% or 70% ratings below.

findings.label: UPS switchover
findings.note: The page lists 'Switching Time: 20 ms' for the UPS-labelled 5-20R outlets only. On 2026-11-15 the store showed 'Sold Out' and 'Price Loading'.

findings.label: Cycle life
findings.source_title: EcoFlow Launches DELTA Pro 3, the Next Generation of Home and Portable Energy Storage (EcoFlow press release, 2024-06-25)
findings.note: Verbatim: 'to last 4000 cycles, exceeding 11 years of usage before reaching 80% capacity'. This is EcoFlow's own release, used because us.ecoflow.com returned HTTP 429. StormWatts gives the same '4,000 to 80%'.

findings.label: AC output
findings.value: 4 kW at 120/240 V from one unit
findings.source_title: EcoFlow Launches DELTA Pro 3 (EcoFlow press release, 2024-06-25)
findings.note: Verbatim: 'a 120/240V 4kW of power output'. No expansion battery is needed for this rating. StormWatts and Offset Solar both say 120 V and 240 V cannot be used at the same time.

findings.label: Measured discharge capacity
findings.source_title: EcoFlow Delta Pro 3 review, Digital Trends (Simon Sage, 2024-06-25)
findings.note: Digital Trends' Simon Sage: 'averaged 3.7 kWh of discharge capacity across multiple cycles'. The review does not describe the load. 3.7 / 4.096 = 0.90.

findings.label: Cycle life
findings.source_title: Jackery Explorer 5000 Plus review: price, specs, catches (OutageReadyHQ)
findings.note: The review's spec table reads '4,000 cycles to 70%+ capacity'. Jackery's product page, FAQ and manual all failed to load (HTTP 429, truncated page, or a PDF with no extractable text), so this comes from a named reviewer copying Jackery's spec. The rating ends at 70% capacity where EcoFlow's ends at 80%, so the same 4,000 cycles promise less remaining capacity than the DELTA Pro 3's.
